global.headline: TRUMP, XI AND PUTIN WILL MEET TOGETHER FOR THE FIRST TIME, TO TALK ABOUT NUCLEAR WEAPONS
summary: The White House said Trump will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin jointly next week on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China — the first trilateral sit-down ever held between the three leaders. The Kremlin says it falls on 19 November in Shenzhen; Beijing has not confirmed it. The stated subject is nuclear non-proliferation: “The President has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world,” said White House spokesman Olivia Wales. Officials played down any outcome. “We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement,” a senior US official said. “I would characterise this as the entry point, the first conversation, certainly at the leader level.” Iran is also on the agenda; whether Ukraine will be is unclear. The last US-Russia arms treaty expired in February and China is expanding its arsenal quickly. Zelenskyy warned last month against “Yalta 2, 3, 4”.
global.geopolitical: Beijing has refused a trilateral arms-control frame since 2019 as unreasonable and unrealistic; turning up concedes the premise even with nothing signed, and puts China's warheads on a table it insists belongs to the two large holders. Moscow's gain is immediate: a leaders' summit while its envoys still refuse Europe a chair at the Ukraine talks.
global.socioeconomic: Shenzhen is also where the tariff file sits: Beijing's suspension of its extra 24 per cent tariff and the pause on its rare-earth controls both expire on 10 January, and what is said about those may matter more than anything said about warheads.

global.headline: WASHINGTON ASKED KYIV WHETHER IT WOULD GIVE UP DONBAS IN RETURN FOR NATO MEMBERSHIP
summary: Zelenskyy told journalists on Friday that American negotiators had put a question never raised before: “What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?” He said Ukraine would not surrender territory, but that with a “comprehensive security package” — a strong army plus NATO and EU guarantees — he would take it to the public. “I have no right to make that decision on my own. But we need specifics, and we don't have them yet.” The question followed the Abu Dhabi round and Kushner and Witkoff's meetings with Putin and with him. Zelenskyy said the American team also pressed a new European security framework, which he read as Russia trying to “redistribute influence in Europe first and foremost”. He added that Starshield restrictions had run five days along the front line and over occupied territory, degrading drone operations; SpaceX denies new limits and calls it a technical issue.
global.geopolitical: NATO enlargement was Putin's stated reason for the 2022 invasion, so offering membership as the price of Donbas inverts the war's own logic — which is why Washington has not confirmed it and Moscow has not answered. Most of Donbas is already Russian-held and the offensive there has stalled, so what would change hands is what Ukraine still holds.
global.socioeconomic: A referendum pledge moves the decision from envoys to voters, and no national vote can be held under martial law. The drones Ukraine flies on Starshield are its cheapest substitute for artillery, so a five-day throttling is a supply shock delivered by a company, not a state.

global.headline: A ROUTER ON A 25-YEAR-OLD NETWORK STOPPED EVERY FLIGHT IN AMERICA
summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday that Friday's nationwide ground stop probably came from contractor L3Harris switching telecommunication lines from copper to fibre at a remote FAA site, with suspect routers in Arkansas and Texas. The new routers flooded others with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, destabilising data at 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centres; none went dark, but the agency could not find a cause and grounded the country. The routers are about 25 years old and were due for replacement in 2006. “We're working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router?” Duffy said; L3Harris said it is supporting the investigation. FAA administrator Bryan Bedford saw “zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related”, and expects full recovery on Sunday. More than 20,000 flights have been disrupted.
global.geopolitical: How much of American airspace one maintenance error can close is now on the record, and so is the single point of failure: “They own this network. They're our prime contractor. I can't go somewhere else,” Duffy said of L3Harris. A capability that cannot be bought elsewhere is a vulnerability whether the next failure is an accident or not.
global.socioeconomic: The FAA spends about US$1 billion a year keeping the copper working, has US$12.5 billion from Congress to replace it and Duffy wants US$50 billion more. Bedford carries the cost: the technology “will continue to break until we replace it”, with 30 per cent of the copper still in place and Thanksgiving travel under two weeks away.

global.headline: AMERICA LOSES ITS MEASLES ELIMINATION STATUS AFTER 26 YEARS
summary: An independent commission reporting to the director of the Pan American Health Organization has determined that the United States no longer qualifies as having eliminated measles, a status held since 2000; the decision was first reported by the Wall Street Journal. A country loses the status when one strain passes person to person for at least a year inside it, judged by sequencing viruses from patients. Utah's public health laboratory showed one strain circulating there for more than a year in an August preprint — over 95 per cent of the state's cases and more than 600 infections between June 2025 and June 2026; outbreaks have also run in South Carolina, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and New York. More than 5,400 cases have been reported this year, the most since 1991, across 43 new outbreaks, with over 1,000 more from outbreaks begun last year. About one in nine reported cases has been hospitalised and at least ten people have died, almost all unvaccinated or of unknown status; two MMR doses cut an exposed person's risk by 97 per cent.
global.geopolitical: The call came from PAHO's commission, not Washington, so a country that led the eradication of smallpox now sits outside a certification it helped build — and any state that traces an imported strain back to the US can now say so.
global.socioeconomic: “Measles elimination is a vital sign for our public health system,” said Demetre Daskalakis, former director of the CDC's immunisation centre. “It shows cracks in our foundation.” Reversing a 65-year-old control programme loads cost onto hospitals through the one in nine cases needing admission, and onto every unvaccinated community the virus now reaches without being imported.

global.headline: ITALY FINES META S$1.1 BILLION FOR TAKING PHOTOS OFF ANDROID PHONES WITHOUT ASKING
summary: Italy's privacy regulator, the Garante, fined Meta €805 million — reported at about US$880 million, roughly S$1.1 billion — after finding that Facebook's Android app reached into users' photos, videos and metadata without specific consent, under the Italian law implementing the EU's ePrivacy directive rather than the GDPR. The feature, “Get suggestions from gallery when browsing Facebook”, offers images from the phone's own gallery while a user scrolls and was switched on by default; about 20 million Italian Android users were affected. The regulator cited Meta's lack of cooperation and a 2019 violation in setting an amount reported at about 0.47 per cent of global turnover. Meta called it disproportionate and will appeal, and has 60 days to turn camera-roll suggestions off by default.
global.geopolitical: Bringing the case under ePrivacy rather than the GDPR routes it through a national regulator instead of Ireland's, where cases against American platforms normally slow to a halt. Other member states will copy that, and it opens a second front while Brussels pursues TikTok's recommender under the Digital Services Act.
global.socioeconomic: The default is the expensive half of the order, not the fine. A gallery permission that must be asked for rather than assumed shrinks the flow of personal images into recommendation and model training — an input Meta has never had to pay for.

global.headline: STARSHIP COMES BACK FROM ORBIT AND IS CAUGHT BY ITS OWN LAUNCH TOWER
summary: SpaceX's Starship upper stage returned from a 22-hour flight on Saturday and descended into the mechanical arms of the tower it had left from at Starbase, Texas — the first time the ship itself, rather than only the booster, has been recovered that way. The 171-foot stage fell out of heavy cloud, reignited three engines to flip vertical and hovered into the “chopstick” arms, charred from reentry. It had circled Earth 14 times on the system's longest mission and deployed 26 Starlink satellites at about 260km before firing an engine to begin a plunge from roughly 17,000mph. The Super Heavy booster that carried it up on Friday failed its own return about ten minutes after liftoff, so both stages have still not been recovered on one mission, and the hexagonal-tile heat shield is not yet reusable without refurbishment.
global.geopolitical: Returning a heavy-lift upper stage to its own launch mount is a capability no state or company has held, and it sits with the firm whose Starshield service Ukraine says is being throttled over the front line, and whose owner flies with the president to meet Xi and Putin this week. Launch capacity on those terms is leverage, not only engineering.
global.socioeconomic: Falcon 9 has flown more than 700 times since 2010 but discards its second stage every flight, the largest remaining cost per launch. Removing it lowers the floor under the price of orbital capacity — for Starlink, and, SpaceX argues, for putting data centres in orbit.

singapore.headline: ASEAN CONCLUDES ITS FIRST BINDING DIGITAL TRADE PACT AS SINGAPORE PREPARES TO TAKE THE CHAIR
summary: The ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement was signed on 14 November by DPM and Trade Minister Gan Kim Yong and his counterparts at the ASEAN Economic Community Council meeting in Manila, closing three years of negotiation. It is the first legally binding regionwide agreement of its kind, setting common rules for digital trade, cross-border data flows and electronic payments across all 11 member states, and is projected to double the region's digital economy from US$1 trillion (S$1.29 trillion) to US$2 trillion by 2030. PM Lawrence Wong arrived the same day for the 49th ASEAN Summit, 15 to 17 November, with Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan. The PMO said leaders will also meet the heads of Australia, China, India, Japan, South Korea, the US and the UN — Trump and Premier Li Qiang among them — with energy security and ratification of the ASEAN Petroleum Security Agreement on the agenda. Marcos hands Wong the gavel on 17 November for Singapore's 2027 chairmanship.
singapore.geopolitical: Binding rules on cross-border data are what ASEAN has never managed to agree, and they arrive while Washington and Beijing write incompatible digital regimes. A single regional standard is the strongest instrument Singapore holds next year against that choice being made one market at a time.
singapore.socioeconomic: For Singapore firms the value is procedural rather than tariff-based: one set of e-payment, data-transfer and digital-trade rules across eleven markets instead of eleven. The doubling projected by 2030 assumes implementation, for which no deadline was announced.

singapore.headline: FULLERTON HEALTH PUTS A NUMBER ON ITS BREACH: 140,000 MIGRANT WORKER RECORDS
summary: About 140,000 work pass holder records were compromised in the Fullerton Health incident, the group and the Ministry of Manpower said in separate statements on 14 November — the first per-organisation figure in the current run of breaches. An unauthorised party reached a standalone server supporting the Migrant Worker Primary Care Plan, potentially exposing names, foreign identification numbers, dates of birth, contact numbers and addresses; about 43,000 records belong to people whose passes are no longer valid. No health, medical or financial information was affected. The group became aware on 31 October, notified MOM on 2 November and the public on 9 November, and is building an entirely new server to host a replacement portal; MOM has written to affected workers in their native languages through the FWMOMCare app. Fullerton is one of four MOM-appointed anchor operators for the plan, which employers must buy for certain work permit and S Pass holders in construction, marine and process work. CSA counts at least 12 incidents involving Singapore organisations or their vendors between 24 October and 13 November, six in healthcare and community care.
singapore.geopolitical: The PDPC's assessment that there is no clear connection between the twelve, with some tied to global breaches, puts much of the exposure in vendor supply chains outside Singapore's jurisdiction. Holding the deploying organisation accountable, as MAS has done for AI, is the only lever that reaches them.
singapore.socioeconomic: The people exposed are the least able to act on it: identification numbers, addresses and phone numbers in one record are the raw material of wage and remittance scams, and the 43,000 whose passes have lapsed are largely out of the country, unreachable through the employers the notifications ran through.

singapore.headline: A FOURTH PERSON DIES ON SINGAPORE'S ROADS IN FOUR DAYS
summary: A 31-year-old motorcyclist died on 14 November after an accident on Jalan Boon Lay towards Jalan Bahar; police and the SCDF were alerted at about 6.50am; he died at Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, and police believe his machine skidded. It is at least the fourth fatal accident in four days, after two separate collisions in which tipper trucks killed cyclists on 11 and 12 November and the death of a 75-year-old man whose power-assisted bicycle hit a car in Hougang on 13 November. Traffic Police mid-year figures put motorcyclists and pillion riders at 45.9 per cent of all traffic deaths and 55.6 per cent of all accidents in the first half of 2026. Injury accidents rose from 3,748 in the first half of 2025 to 3,869, and people hurt from 4,894 to 5,090. Road deaths reached 149 in 2025, a decade high.
singapore.geopolitical: Four deaths in four days across three vehicle types is not the rider-behaviour story enforcement has concentrated on. It is an argument about road design and vehicle mix — heavy construction traffic sharing lanes with two-wheelers — which the Traffic Police's split between riders and everyone else does not describe.
singapore.socioeconomic: Riders and pillion passengers are about half the casualties while being a small fraction of road users, concentrated in work where the vehicle is the job. Rising injuries on a decade-high death toll is a cost carried by households and hospital capacity, not a transport budget line.

word.definition: A group of three people or powers acting together, especially in government or negotiation; originally a Russian carriage drawn by three horses abreast.
word.etymology: From Russian тройка (troika), from tri, “three”. It entered English in the nineteenth century for the three-horse sleigh, and took on its political sense after the Soviet leadership arrangements of the 1920s and again in 1953, when power was shared among three men following Stalin's death.
word.example: A nuclear troika has never met before: Trump, Xi and Putin are expected in Shenzhen on 19 November, and American officials are already saying no agreement should be expected.
